summary: A set of choices of which one can be chosen. It is one form control and one stop in the Tab order.

value.description: The value of the chosen radio. With none written, the group takes the radio the author marked as checked.

name.description: The name the value is submitted under.

required.description: The form cannot be submitted while no radio is chosen.

orientation.description: horizontal puts the radios in a row.

disabled.description: It cannot be changed or focused.

variant.description: segmented joins the radios into one control of segments, each a label with no mark.

root.note: Stacks its radios and paints nothing. Segmented, it is one recessed track as tall as a control, and gives its ink to the segments.

thumb.note: Segmented only: the raised face of the checked segment, never the solid face. It takes the box of the checked segment, its anchor, and moves to the next one checked (C32). Drawn as a pseudo-element, so it is in place before the elements are defined. A plain group generates none.

keys.ArrowDown, ArrowRight: Move focus to the next radio and choose it; wrap at the end.
keys.ArrowUp, ArrowLeft: The same, to the previous radio.
keys.Space: Chooses the radio that has focus.
keys.Tab: Enters the group at the chosen radio, or at the first when none is chosen, and chooses nothing.

events.input: Dispatched when the user chooses another radio.

guidance.text: The author names the group with aria-label or aria-labelledby.
Write `checked` on the chosen radio, so that it is painted before the group is defined.
Write `variant="segmented"` on the group alone: its radios are painted as the segments of one track, in a row, before either element is defined. The keys, the roles and the form value do not change.
A segmented group is a row whatever its orientation; write `orientation="horizontal"` as well so that assistive technology hears a row. Keep it to a few short labels: segments do not wrap.

notYet: A segmented group that is disabled still shows the hover face of a segment under the pointer, as a plain one tints the well.
The hit area of a segment reaches over the kit's track padding, not over a padding set with `--radio-group-inset`.
